title: White Dwarf
body:
A **white dwarf** is the exposed core left behind when a low-mass star sheds its outer layers.
It is roughly the mass of the Sun compressed into the volume of Earth, giving densities around
a tonne per cubic centimetre.

Nothing is fusing inside it. It is held up by electron degeneracy pressure, a quantum effect
where electrons resist being packed into the same state, and that support is independent of
temperature. A white dwarf therefore has no fuel to run out of and simply radiates its stored
heat away over billions of years, cooling and fading.

On the [[HR Diagram]] it sits at the bottom left, hot and dim, which the
[[Blackbody Radiation]] laws explain: the surface is very hot and there is very little of
it.

The **Chandrasekhar limit** of about 1.4 solar masses is where degeneracy pressure fails. Above
it, gravity wins and the collapse continues past the white dwarf stage, which is why no white
dwarf heavier than that has ever been found.

That limit is also what makes a Type Ia [[Supernova]] a standard candle. A white dwarf in a
[[Binary Stars|binary]] can pull material from its companion until it crosses the limit,
and the resulting explosion always happens at the same mass, so it always releases about the
same energy. Knowing the luminosity turns the [[Inverse-Square Law]] into a distance
measurement, and that is what carried the distance ladder to cosmological range.
